_comment: RAM budgets for stemtape_player, enforced by
stemtape_player_ram_inventory.py against the linked ELF.
These are RATCHETS, not aspirations: each is set at or just above what
the image actually uses, so any growth fails the build and has to be
argued for in a diff. They come DOWN as the audit reclaims memory; they
do not go up without a stated reason in the commit that raises them.
TARGET, recorded here so it is not lost: 98304 bytes free (96 KiB), which
the analysis in src/st_latency.h shows is reachable only with a unified
sector cache at the adopted latency guarantee. min_free_bytes tracks what
is currently PROVEN, not the target.
fx: the one FX rack. 36864 is a RATCHET just above the 32,952 the rack
actually occupies -- 32,768 of it the single echo delay line. It is a
separate category precisely so the rack cannot hide inside the general
'stemtape' allowance: a second rack, or a stereo delay line, fails here.
transfer: 0, and that is the ratchet, not an accident. Its only member
was the 8,192-byte upload verify scratch, which as of st38 has no
allocation of its own -- it is the last loop-pin buffer, behind the
quiesce handshake. The category is kept at zero so the moment anything
is classified 'transfer' again the build fails and the reclamation has
to be re-argued rather than quietly undone. See _reclaimed in
ram-ownership.json for the full account, including why the read-ahead
ring was the wrong donor.
min_free_bytes is deliberately NOT ratcheted up by what Stage A returned
(9,088 B measured). It is earmarked: the v1.2 planar read path spends
8,192 on per-stem rings at G=7/R=3 (docs/stem-tape-v1.2-planar-format.md),
landing at 34,466 free -- 1,698 above this floor. Raising the floor now
and lowering it two commits later would record motion, not progress.
That 1,698 B is the whole remaining margin, so a growth that passes this
gate today can still make the planar read path unshippable. Check the
table in stem-tape-ram-v1.md before adding anything large.
